validation_changes: Per-pass RPM logs now require unique labels, successful status, valid bounded addresses, exact byte lengths, and matching SHA-256.
Static source pins and runtime code-guard records are checked against the pinned profile and RPM trace bytes.
Game/date/country/sailor/cache-state values and country database/table/count/match rows are bound to trace bytes; country matches are rebuilt including slot high-16-bit validation.
Dense modifier IDs bind to individual RPM rows; sparse first-match and absent-zero values are rebuilt from complete entry traces.
Processor manager/global/slot pointers bind to trace bytes, and force_limits is recomputed from signed 32-bit inputs and processor slots before comparison with the public field.
A cache state of 1 preserves the known sailors result while requiring both force subfields to remain unknown.
Capture RPM byte and call totals are checked against the two pass read logs.
counterexamples: Self-consistent simultaneous sailors value/raw/hex/display tampering is rejected.
Self-consistent force count/raw/hex tampering is rejected.
Dense modifier raw-ID versus trace and sparse duplicate-ID first-match contradictions are rejected.
A non-null processor slot cannot be relabelled as null.
limits: This is synthetic/offline validation only; no target process, game, MCP, or new RPM capture was used.
No freeze, repository-wide test run, or live validation was performed.
Failed/incomplete RPM traces remain fail-closed at record validation; this review does not establish that arbitrary force-read errors preserve sailors availability.
Force-limit semantics remain partial and do not execute dynamic processors or establish game cache freshness.
